r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Before recording pass, fill this item's postcondition command with the real record path you wrote it to -- record() now runs it and refuses `pass` if it fails. Do NOT silently skip this item.

postconditions.statement: verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0 on the Fowler-pass record -- refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override

constraints: Fowler smells are subordinate to documented repo standards; never hard violations
an override (smell not flagged because a standard wins) needs a logged reason
r6-fowler.finding: Fowler pass driven and rail-verified. Record: .agent-work/epic418-h-447/g2-review/fowler-pass.json; 'python scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/epic418-h-447/g2-review/fowler-pass.json' EXIT=0 (smells=12, flagged=['message-chains'], overridden=[long-method, duplicated-code, shotgun-surgery, divergent-change, comments-as-deodorant]). I also proved the rail can fail rather than trusting its green: dropping feature-envy => exit 1 'skipped baseline smell'; stripping shotgun-surgery's override block => exit 1 'OVERRIDE-LOG'. Five overrides each cite a specific documented standard; notably shotgun-surgery (hardcoding ACTIVE_DIR rather than importing the writer is real duplication, but importing it is exactly what constraint:episodes-are-not-prescriptions forbids - a settled/human anchor is not mine to unsettle for a refactoring preference) and comments-as-deodorant (the heavy prose is mandated by Tommy's standing scope-discipline ruling and carries design intent the code cannot express; my mutation testing confirmed the CODE enforces the valve, not the prose).

r3d.title: CC4: sentinel valve test + my own injected-leak red proof
r3d.imperative: Inject my own leak into scan_episode(), confirm the sentinel test goes RED, restore byte-identically, verify restore and green.

r4d.title: Constraint: declined corner cases carry a comment AT the stated file:line
r4d.imperative: Verify each of the four declined corner cases the implementer names actually has its comment at the stated location.
r4d.finding: All four declined corner cases carry their comment AT the stated file:line - I read each location, none was a paraphrase pointing elsewhere. (1) scripts/verify_episode_captured.py:196-201, the --store-root default installed-copy hazard, sitting directly above the 'root = ...' line it describes. (2) scripts/verify_episode_captured.py:151-161, _git_tracked cannot distinguish untracked from not-a-repository, in that function's own docstring. (3) scripts/verify_episode_captured.py:125-130, retired/ deliberately not searched, immediately above the active.glob loop. (4) scripts/apply_episode_delta.py:511-522, the store_root() hazard, and the docstring's durable_root() ruling above it is byte-unchanged. Each names the case, why it was not chased, and what closes it. This is the sanctioned exit under Tommy's scope-discipline ruling and it was taken correctly.

r4e.title: Constraint: the valve — episodes are a record, not a playbook
r4e.imperative: Read the implementation for any path that could surface statement text or read the store as a rule source.
r4e.finding: The valve holds under adversarial probing, not just by construction. Three independent lines of attack. (i) STRUCTURAL: ast parse shows stdlib-only imports, no query_episodes, no repo-local module, no dynamic-import escape hatch - the module physically cannot reach a store reader. (ii) BEHAVIOURAL: I seeded my OWN sentinel (REVIEWER-SENTINEL-LEAK-CANARY-7c31) into every assertion statement of every episode in 10 throwaway stores and ran the gate as a subprocess across all outcome paths - captured, blocked, other-runs-only, archive-blocked, archive-passed, refused-missing-root, refused-missing-active, refused-malformed, feedback-on-untracked, relative-root-archive. Sentinel present in stdout or stderr: FALSE on all 10. (iii) MECHANISTIC: the read boundary is the protection, not the print statements. scan_episode breaks before '## Agent-supplied', so statement bytes are never in memory; my mutation A leaked every line the function reads and the sentinel test stayed green, because there is nothing sensitive there to leak. Emitted surface is ids, counts, paths and git's own diagnostics - no statement, no ripeness, no counters, no dormancy, no apply-or-defer. constraint:episodes-are-not-prescriptions is honoured, and it is now enforced by a test with a working red proof rather than by prose.

triage_candidates.statement: Reviewer survey template gap: skills/reviewer/templates/REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json ships r6-fowler with an UNFILLED postcondition placeholder 'python scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <fowler-pass-record-path>'. Its own imperative orders the reviewer to 'fill this item's postcondition command with the real record path', but the engine exposes no verb to do that (amend is gated-only) while global-everyone.md forbids hand-editing the work file. The only way through is a raw edit of the check command, which on Windows ALSO risks rewriting all 371 CRLF line endings if done with text I/O. Fix options: have verify_fowler_pass.py default to a conventional path, or teach the engine to substitute a per-run token, or have the reviewer skill instruct filling placeholders BEFORE claim.

docs/agents/engine-config.json does not exist, yet every checklist in this work area names it as config_ref (g1's review, g2's crew plans, this survey). The engine silently accepts the dangling reference, so rework cap and human-checkpoint policy are running on built-in defaults nobody chose. Independently confirmed: 'ls docs/agents/' returns CREW_CONTEXT.md, GLOSSARY.md, ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md only. Same finding the g2 implementer raised.

tests/test_mutation_floor.py:255's harness regex FAILED (tests[/\]test_map_orient\.py::\S+) cannot match when the environment forces colour, because pytest emits an ANSI reset between FAILED and the node id. Measured: 'python -m pytest -q' exits 1 with 10 HARNESS ERROR failures under this session's FORCE_COLOR, and 'FORCE_COLOR=0 NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q' exits 0 with 1715 passed. The Commander root-caused it for this run but no fix is filed: the harness should strip ANSI or pin FORCE_COLOR=0 for its own nested pytest, otherwise this class permanently masks any real regression in that file.

Both the g2 IMPLEMENTER_RESULT and the g2 REVIEWER_HANDOFF state 'tests/test_verify_episode_captured.py - 16 tests', and the result states the script is '223 lines'. Measured: 'pytest --collect-only -q' reports 15 tests collected (exit 0) and 'wc -l' reports 245. Cosmetic, no behavioural impact, but it is a count carried in prose that was never re-derived from a command - the exact shape global-everyone.md 'Pin a claim to the revision you read it at' warns about.
